Together with some friends I opened 16 boxes. Rarity distribution was
fine, with a very even distribution of rares and uncommons for
everyone.

For some boxes I took notes of the rares. In all those boxes we had 36
different rares.

Generelly I think it is a good idea to "pool" your boxes with some
friends. I have done this for years. Normally we put all the rares
together and distribute them evenly, depending on the sets the
uncommons and vampires as well. This really saves a lot of trading...

Messages.Author: John P.
Messages.Body:
"LSJ" <vte...@white-wolf.com> wrote in message news:VPy0l.10403> Corners:

Unmasking, NRA Pact, Heart of the City, Ivory Bow.
>
> Enkil is on an edge (other cards on the same edge: Unmasking, Charisma,
> Anarch Troublemaker, Aaron's Feeding Razor, Blood Weakens, Specialization,
> New Management, Renegade Garou, and NRA PAC).

Wow... so one of my boxes was totally edge:

In order of boosters opened, starting with the 10th booster down on the lef
side of the box I received: Charisma, Anarch Troublemaker, Aaron's Feeding
razor, Blood Weakens, Enkil Cog, Specialization, New Management, Renegade
Garou, and NRA PAC and unmasking appeared later on.

In both boxes of boosters commons were organized into repeated 5 card sets.
Commons never appeared outside of these sets, and always in the same order.
Not a terrible thing for commons I guess but if its indicative throughout
the set, it will make drafting interesting.

Vampires appear to be occuring in runs of the same order, although not
always in sync. (Eg in one booster received A,B,C next received D,E,F....
later in box vampires were B,C,D, then E,F,G etc). Makes for less duplicate
vamps I guess.

I'm also noticing common strings of rares in order. Will know more once I
finish recording the booster contenets for my second box.

-John P.
Winnipeg
